concepts.title: The Ever-Evolving World of Science
concepts.definition: Science never stands still: from cells inside a leaf to the motion of sun and stars, each answered question opens new ones, and the subject keeps evolving with every experiment we dare to try.
concepts.key_idea: Science is a moving frontier: questions are its fuel and experiments its engine.
question_patterns: why is science called ever evolving
what does the textbook invite us to do
name two very different scales science studies
how do new answers create new questions
give one example of science changing with time
why should we question the answers we get

concepts.title: Questioning the Answer
concepts.definition: The activity 'Question the Answer' flips the usual order: take a settled statement and poke it with fresh questions, asking why, how and what if, exactly as working scientists do.
concepts.key_idea: Answered questions are doors, not walls: good questioning keeps science alive.
question_patterns: how do we question an answer
why should answers be questioned again
frame three questions about why the sky is blue
what happens to science when questioning stops
which answer of grade 6 surprised you on rechecking
turn one textbook statement into three questions

concepts.title: From Small Cells to Far Stars
concepts.definition: Science studies everything from tiny cells inside a leaf to the movement of the sun and stars; the same habits of observing, experimenting and reasoning work at every scale.
concepts.key_idea: Scale does not change the method: small or far, nature answers the same careful questions.
question_patterns: name the smallest things science studies
name the farthest things science studies
what is common between studying cells and stars
which instruments help us see very small things
how do we study objects too far to visit
why does one method work at all scales

concepts.title: Happy Exploring: The Year Ahead
concepts.definition: The chapter closes with a welcome to explore: substances and colours, electricity, metals, changes, life processes, light, heat, time and the sky, each chapter a fresh expedition for the curious.
concepts.key_idea: A science textbook is a travel guide: every chapter is a place to visit and question.

which chapter are you most curious about and why
how is this textbook different from a book of facts
what does happy exploring mean to you
how will you keep a record of your explorations
why does exploring need both reading and doing
